answer: An agent economy resists sybils by giving each person one anonymous credential and revealing only a nullifier per use. Enrollment grants one secret per human; a nullifier derives from it, so two accounts of one person collide and the ledger rejects the second — an anchor of one-person-one-secret needing no deanonymization. Splitting into N keys fails: N nullifiers from one secret collide, forcing N humans. The scarce resource is one-per-human issuance, a ferrous registry refusing repeats; a garden of clones grows only with real people. Linear cost deters cheap minting, not a wealthy recruiter.
